notes.title: Celebrating our 5th anniversary and Six Million Players!
notes.content:
[h2]Hey Riders,[/h2]

Lonely Mountains: Downhill turns 5 years old today and today we also crossed 6 million players on the leaderboards! Even after 5 years, the game is still alive and kicking and we are tremendously grateful for that. 

When we started LMD in the Summer of 2015 it was a hobby mobile game project that we did for fun in our spare time. Not in our wildest dreams would we have imagined that it would find its way into the hands of so many players.

For the last 10 years, Lonely Mountains has been our life and what once started as a 2-person pet project has now grown into a 14-person company. We are incredibly thankful for having the privilege to work every day on something we love (and still be able to pay our bills).  

We are looking forward to the next 5 years with you and as always wish you a great ride on the Lonely Mountains!

Jan, Daniel & The Megagons

PS: If you’re looking for a birthday present it would be great if you could leave a positive review for either LMD or the Snow Riders demo!

notes.title: Snow Riders multiplayer demo out now!
notes.content:
[h2]Hey Riders[/h2]

A huge thanks to everyone who tried the teaser demo for Lonely Mountains: Snow Riders already! Your feedback is super helpful and it's good to see our speed-running community already doing the most crazy runs!😀

Today, we launched the full demo for Lonely Mountains: Snow Riders with a huge update that adds the following:
[list]
[*] 2-8 online multiplayer (racing)
[*] Added a whole new mountain track to explore (single and multiplayer)
[*] Improved physics. We took your feedback to heart and tweaked the physics a little bit. Initial pushing is now stronger, less air resistance at low speeds but stronger resistance at higher speeds and landing sidewards is more forgiving now.
[*] Due to the new balancing, we also cleared the leaderboards because previous records might not be achievable anymore. 
[*] Tons of fixes and improvements but most importantly
[*] - The infinite loading screen should be gone
[*] - The crash some people experienced when starting the game should now also be fixed
[/list]

You can download the demo on our demo Steam page right now!
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3238120/Lonely_Mountains_Snow_Riders_Demo/

This is the first time we are testing our online multiplayer, and we are super curios to hear if you like it! This time we are testing the racing mode for up to 8 people but the full version will also have a co-op mode. The team already had the best time testing the racing mode, as going on the slopes with a few friends adds a ton of fun and competitive chaos!

We are likely leaving the demo up for the whole duration of the Steam Fest (until the 21st October) but might remove it afterward again for a while to polish it up. So jump in while it lasts! 🙂

[previewyoutube=qwv3ImIALEA;full][/previewyoutube]

If you enjoy Lonely Mountains: Snow Riders, please add it to your wishlist or follow our developer account as that helps us a lot to make the game more visible on Steam. We would also be super grateful if you leave a review for the demo. 

All the best and have a great ride on the snowy Lonely Mountains!

Your Megagons

notes.title: Announcing Lonely Mountains: Snow Riders!
notes.content:
Hello Riders!

Since we launched Lonely Mountains: Downhill five years ago, we’ve had lots of questions about what’s coming next. Now we can finally tell you!

[b]Please welcome Lonely Mountains: Snow Riders - our snowy follow-up to Lonely Mountains: Downhill[/b]
[previewyoutube=nPV7r1RY5bY;full][/previewyoutube]

The [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2545360/Lonely_Mountains_Snow_Riders/]Steam Page[/url] is now live, so please check it out for more info and be sure to wishlist! You can also join our [url=https://discord.gg/lonelymountains]discord[/url] for more news, including info on our upcoming playtests.

Like Downhill, Snow Riders is all about finding a sense of peace and freedom in beautiful environments while challenging your skills. We’re proud to say this game really captures the “feel” of skiing, whether it be cutting through deep powder snow, skittering across the ice or flying over a death-defying jump.

Maybe the most exciting thing of all, Snow Riders adds a brand new element to the Lonely Mountains universe – multiplayer! The online multiplayer mode can be played with up to 8 people and includes both  a versus mode and a more chill collab mode where you share checkpoints and ski down together.

notes.title: Start of Season 32 - Fullmetal Rider Recap & Season Plan 2024
notes.content:
[h2]Hello Riders,[/h2]

We hope you’re all doing well. Today is the start of season 32, which is a recap of Season 20 - Fullmetal Rider. It’s one of our favorite seasons, featuring all a mechanical heart can wish for. 

But we would also like to take some time to inform you about our Daily Rides plans for this year. Because for the foreseeable future, every upcoming season will be a recap season. 

There are a couple of reasons for this decision. Most importantly, as you might already know, we’re working on a new game (which we hope we can tell you all about soon) so we need all hands on deck for the new game. 

But also, with our last new season “Knights on Bikes” we now have 20 unique seasons. This is by far more than we ever dreamed of when we started the Daily Rides and we never would have thought that we would still be adding new content to the game four and a half years after release. We want to thank you all for keeping this game alive for so long!

But a lot of current players have never seen any of the past seasons and would love to get their hands on the existing season items. So we think we have reached the point where it just makes sense to put more of the recap seasons into rotation rather than creating a new season.

On the plus side, this also means that we don’t have to worry about spoiling new seasons anymore. Therefore we decided to announce the full season plan for this year so that everyone can also plan ahead. As always, there will still be a weeklong break between each season. Here is the season plan:

notes.title: Daily Rides Season 16 - Cirque du vélo
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Riders,[/h1]

Welcome back to Season 16 of our Daily Rides! We hope you’re all doing well. This season the circus is coming to town so please stand up and give warm applause to our Cirque du vélo!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30570088/9a896ec38b7540bc1559b3cb752aee247835bb0e.jpg[/img]

This season not only comes with a whole bunch of stunning circus outfits and accessories, but we also introduce some changes to the Daily Ride structure. From now on Daily Rides will follow a weekly plan, so that each day a specific modifier or mode will always be active.

The plan goes as follows:

[list]
[*] Mirrored Monday - Mirror modifier will be active.
[*] Night-Time Tuesday - Night mode will be active.
[*] Winning Wednesday - Score Multiplier modifier will be active (and only on this day)
[*] Freeride Thursday - Freeride will always be active.
[*] Fast Friday - Unlimited Sprinting modifier will be active.
[*] Reckless Saturday - No Penalty modifier will be active.
[*] Super Sunday - Super Bike modifier will be active.
[/list]

These fixed modifiers (except the Score Multiplier) can be combined with other random modifiers, so they can still appear more than once. As an example, there could still be an active Super Bike and Mirror modifier on Fast Friday. 

From now on our DLC trails from Eldfjall Island, Riley’s Return, and Misty Peak will also be a part of the normal trail selection. This way they will be part of the Daily Rides way more often than they have been in the past. You don’t need to own the DLCs to play them in the Daily Rides - but of course, owning them helps with training for the Daily Rides ;)

As always the season will run for one month and will end on the 14th of September. Please let us know what you think of the new season and the daily ride changes in our [url=https://discord.gg/lonelymountains]Discord.[/url]

We wish you a great ride and a happy new season!

notes.title: Lonely Mountains: Downhill's new Daily Ride modifiers add Mirrored Mode and more

Developer Megagon Industries' wonderfully serene (and deliciously infuriating) mountain bike adventure Lonely Mountains: Downhill is a brilliant thing, but given that it's also a year and a half old now, fans may be hoping for a bit of a shake-up. And what do you know? Megagon's newest update is here to do just that, wafting away the threat of encroaching staleness with a range of new Daily Ride challenge modifiers.

Daily Rides, if you've not yet checked them out, are daily cross-platform leaderboards that challenge players to do their best in a randomly selected trial, with participants able to unlock various cosmetic rewards, refreshed each season, along the way. Today's update marks the start of Lonely Mountains' seventh season, Summer Strolls, and introduces those aforementioned modifiers to freshen things up for players.

Today's Daily Ride, for instance, rolls out the new Changed Checkpoints modifier - which, as its name suggests, changes and adds new checkpoints to the trail - but future modifiers for the season have also been revealed (and you can see a few of them in the trailer below).

notes.title: Up Close: Mountains, mindfulness, and metaphysics: the supreme realism of Lonely Mountains: Downhill and A Short Hike
notes.content:
Up Close is a new, occasional and informal series here on Eurogamer, looking at the smaller points in games in greater amounts of depth. Covering anything from a single mechanic to a reoccurring theme, in praise or criticism, the aim is simply to look a little closer at the things that deserve our attention.

Increasingly, games are looking to the environment to tell their stories. It's easy enough to see why. On one side the natural world is moving closer and closer to the centre of our thought, as the climate crisis becomes more urgent and less easy to ignore. On the other, it becomes a great device for telling a story of impending, existential disaster - or indeed one of the hope to be found in the aftermath. And, above all, pretty environments sell.

But alongside the rise of environmentally aware games is a little micro-surge of environmentally conscious ones. Which is to say, games that are less about the environment as they are about that way you think about it, the connection that forms between your mind and the world around you. Metaphysics, basically, or mindfulness, if we want to narrow it down further. In particular I'm thinking of a couple of mindfulness games from the end of last year, Lonely Mountains: Downhill and A Short Hike, which both look to use the natural world to turn your own gaze inwards, and both happen to use mountains - specifically going either up a mountain or down one, although there aren't many other things to do with mountains in fairness - to achieve the kind of effect I think they're after.

notes.title: Games of the Year 2019: Lonely Mountains: Downhill is a magic game of pure sensation
notes.content:
Over the festive break we'll be running through our top 20 picks of the year's best games, leading up to the reveal of Eurogamer's game of the year on New Year's Eve. You can find all the pieces published to date here - and thanks for joining us throughout the year!

Sometimes, playing Lonely Mountains: Downhill, I can't help but think the aim of the game is to stop playing it. On the surface this is a game about going downhill fast, about beating the clock, cutting corners, sprinting. The race to the finish often ends in a rush of relief, above all, that you've made it there intact. And then at the same time it's the absolute opposite: tranquility, calm, an invitation to stay a while and just listen. At once you're baited into crashing through it and challenged into slowing down for a ponder.

I could, honestly, leave it there. Lonely Mountains' tug-of-war between styles of play is enough in itself, the game a clever little buried lede of one kinetic, mechanical thing on the surface (timers, challenges, sprint buttons, checkpoints) and another, more contemplative, just beneath (crunching leaves, branching paths, hidden oases with fallen trunks to sit on and views to be quietly taken in). But there is so, so much more going on here. Lonely Mountains is, above all, a game about experience - about the act of experiencing, in fact - and played through that lens it's not just clever, it's divine.

Brilliant indie biking game Lonely Mountains: Downhill has announced a festive event for the holiday season - and if you haven't played it yet, now's a good time to quickly tell you why.

notes.title: Lonely Mountains: Downhill bikes on down to Kickstarter
notes.content:
As a child, I always loved the idea of downhill cycling; the rush of the wind, feeling every bump in the ground beneath you, the thrill of weaving between dangers. The reality was never quite as kind. Turns out that in order to ride down a hill, you have to climb up it first. Then there’s the faceplants, the blood and the mud.

Young Dominic learned to stick to flat, clear roads.

As flawed as the reality was, I still hold a place in my heart for that platonic ideal, never quite realised, so I find myself drawn towards Lonely Mountains: Downhill, a game (now seeking funding through Kickstarter) aiming to capture at least some of the spirit of clinging to a two-wheeled metal frame while hurtling down a mountain at dangerous speeds.
